A distinguishable configuration of a system at a declared descriptive level.
A state encoded inside another system or model for subsequent comparison, prediction, control, or interpretation.
A distinguishable non-identity between two declared states or values.
A declared ordered or unordered connection between distinguishable states, objects, or events.
A relation whose source, target, direction, or transformation order is part of the object.
A condition that restricts the admissible states, transitions, or trajectories of a system.
A declared distinction separating a system-relative inside from outside or one admissible region from another.
A rule mapping admissible input states or relations to output states or relations.
An application of an operator or transition rule that changes a state or relation.
An ordered sequence of states connected by transitions; the path is part of the represented object.
A declared measurable or computable quantity associated with a state, relation, or trajectory.
A property preserved under a declared class of admissible transformations.
A single-valued quantity in a declared scalar domain.
An ordered multi-component object transforming under a declared vector-space or coordinate rule.
A multilinear or coordinate-covariant object with transformation law declared by the model.
A rule assigning relational distance or discrepancy subject to its declared mathematical properties.
A space locally described by coordinates and transition maps, used only when the required smooth/topological structure is declared.
A map from a richer state description to a reduced representation; projection-dependent quantities are not automatically invariants.
A concrete physical, biological, or computational implementation of an abstract object; realization is not identity by definition.
The declared evidential class of a statement: definition, derived result, implemented object, validated result, hypothesis, interpretation, speculative extension, or deprecated claim.
A distinguishable difference available at a declared descriptive level; information alone does not imply meaning or consciousness.
Information whose system-relevant content is specified by how differences constrain, update, or transform other states and relations.
A distinguishable ordered relation between represented states together with declared strength, phase, direction, and transformation history.
A state specified by the organized relations among represented components rather than by component labels alone.
For PhaseNav states V,Q, the squared complex-overlap magnitude R(V,Q)=|d^-1 sum_j exp(i(Q_j-V_j))|^2; more generally, a declared measure of organized relational alignment.
The argument Theta(V,Q) of the complex relational overlap z(V,Q).
A TIR working action S_rel(V,Q)=-kappa log(R(V,Q)+epsilon), converting relational loss to an accumulated information-scale cost.
The fixed scale kappa=ln(2)/(24*pi), used as an informational normalization in the current formalism.
The relevance a represented state has for a particular system given its self-anchor, boundary, goals, valuation, and history.
The system-relative organization produced by the subjectivity transform: information as relevant for this system now, not merely extant information.
A circular coordinate defined modulo its declared period; phase is not by itself a mental or conscious variable.
The oriented or unoriented difference between two phases under a declared wrapping convention.
A declared measure of phase alignment across components or time; the specific estimator must be stated.
Enhanced relational response or alignment under compatible dynamical conditions; resonance is not synonymous with consciousness, truth, love, or ethics.
A declared dependence by which the evolution of one component influences another.
Time-extended tendency of coupled systems to approach stable phase or frequency relations.
A state or process of bounded relative phase/frequency alignment under a declared criterion.
A regime in which relative phase remains bounded or constant within a declared tolerance.
Systematic change of relative phase over time.
A change of phase coordinate by a declared angular increment.
A change in resultant amplitude or relational response caused by combination of phase-bearing components; interpretation depends on the realization.
Satisfaction of a declared return, periodicity, holonomy, or consistency condition after a path or transformation sequence.
The residual mismatch from a declared phase-closure condition.
The transformation accumulated around or along an ordered path; physical gauge holonomy and cognitive path residue must be explicitly distinguished.
In the qualia model, the ordered residue H_gamma_t=T_{t-1->t} o ... o T_{0->1} by which present organization depends on the path used to reach it; no physical gauge field is implied.
A geometric phase associated with parallel transport in a declared state-space bundle or projective-state model.
